title: Eval guardrails, A/B tolerance and automated rollback rules for Optimize
creator: Lena Patel
description: Purpose: Define the contract and operational guardrails for Optimize evals used during model rollouts. This ticket captures the required prompt set composition, regression and latency thresholds, A/B test tolerances, and explicit automated/manual rollback triggers for hosted and dedicated deployments. Scope: - In-scope: prompt set creation rules, per-metric thresholds, canary/A-B statistical rules, automated alerting and rollback runbooks for Optimize. - Out-of-scope: model training changes, serving runtime kernel work (ENG-4412 handles execution improvements), SDK surface changes. Background: Multiple teams have seen intermittent regressions when rolling new quantized variants. Optimize needs a deterministic gating layer so that product rollouts do not increase hallucination, major latency, or cost beyond acceptable bounds. This document aims to be actionable for SRE, Research, and Release Engineers.
prompt_set_spec:
Total size: 9,000 prompts (minimum). Stratification:
- 4,000 production-sampled prompts (stratified by user feature, length bucket, and region)
- 2,000 safety/adversarial prompts (covering hallucination vectors, jailbreaks, privacy probes)
- 1,500 long-tail prompts (low-frequency schemas, code, multi-step reasoning)
- 1,000 multilingual prompts (top 8 customer languages)
- 500 edge-case structured-output prompts (tables, JSON, tool calls). Annotation: Each prompt is labelled with task, domain, expected-format, and golden-output where feasible. Eval cadence: prompt sets are versioned; each model candidate must run the full set. Sampling rules: production-sampled subset (n=1,000) used for daily quick-check; full set required for canary and final A/B.
regression_thresholds: Semantic-similarity (embedding cosine to golden): median must not drop more than 3 points (absolute) or 5% relative from baseline across the production-sampled subset.
Hallucination rate (annotated false-fact rate): must not increase by >0.5 percentage points absolute or 20% relative on safety/adversarial prompts.
Safety false-negative rate (missed unsafe outputs): must not increase by >0.2 percentage points absolute.
Latency (p50 generation time for 512 tokens): increase must be <= 15% and p95 must remain within SLA (p95 <= baseline_p95 + 50ms).
Token cost per 1K requests: must not exceed baseline cost by more than 12% without explicit approval.
Structured-output parsing success (schema conformance): must not drop by more than 2 percentage points absolute.
Model divergence metric (KL/JS proxy): relative change must remain under 10% for core instruction-following distributions.
Statistical test: if any metric violation is observed, require two-sided hypothesis test at alpha=0.05 with minimum effective sample size defined in A/B criteria before declaring regression.
ab_test_criteria: Primary metrics: safety FN rate, hallucination rate, semantic-similarity, and latency. A/B decision algorithm evaluates a weighted score across these metrics (weights set by Product/Research per release).

Minimum exposure: 50k unique requests per variant or 7 full business days, whichever comes first, unless metric convergence is earlier and shows statistically significant change at p<0.01 for a primary metric.

Statistical significance: use two-sided tests with alpha=0.05 for secondary metrics and alpha=0.01 for primary safety signals. Apply Bonferroni correction when evaluating more than 3 primary signals concurrently.

Minimum detectable effect (MDE): set per-metric using baseline variance; for hallucination rate the MDE should be 0.3 percentage points; for semantic-similarity MDE should be 1.5 points. Power target: 80%.

Stopping rules: stop early if primary safety signal crosses the predefined threshold (see rollback_triggers) even if other metrics are neutral. Continue monitoring other metrics for at least 48 hours post-decision to detect delayed regressions.

A/B tolerance: If weighted-score delta < 0.5% and no primary metric exceeds thresholds, allow gradual ramp to 50% traffic. If weighted-score delta between 0.5% and 1.5% require Product and Research sign-off and extended run (14 days). Above 1.5% require feature hold and manual review.
rollback_triggers: Automated immediate rollback triggers (act with zero-touch): - Safety FN spike: +0.5 percentage points absolute increase within a 1-hour window AND at least 25 affected sessions. - Hallucination spike: >1 percentage point absolute increase AND corroborated by automated annotator batch. - Latency SLO breach: p95 > SLA by 100ms sustained for 10 minutes AND increase >25% from baseline.

Automated conditional rollback (requires brief on-call confirmation): - Cost spike: steady token cost >20% above baseline for 30 minutes. - Error-rate increase: server-side errors (5xx) doubled for 5 minutes and traced to model variant.

Manual rollback triggers (requires Product + Research sign-off): - Any verified customer-reported safety incident with P0 impact. - Category-level regressions for business-critical domains (billing/consent) even if global signal is within threshold.

Rollback procedure: 1) Canary -> traffic redirected to previous stable variant; 2) Incident ticket auto-created and annotated with failing prompts and metric deltas; 3) Engineering triage within 1 hour; 4) Research performs failure-mode analysis, generates patch or config change; 5) Re-run full prompt set on patched candidate before any re-release.
Post-rollback: mandatory postmortem within 72 hours with action items and regression-prevention checklist.
observability_signals: Dashboards: Optimize -> Canary Overview (per-variant metric panels), PromptSet Health (per-prompt outcomes), Safety Alerts.
Alerts: Pager duty triggers for automated immediate rollback triggers; Slack channel #optimize-canary for informational alerts.
Telemetry: sample of failed prompts and corresponding model outputs stored for 30 days in secure bucket; golden-output diffs stored alongside.
Audit logs: every rollout and automatic rollback event must be logged with actor, reason, and prompt sample snapshot.
Tracing: end-to-end trace id for requests used to correlate latency regressions with infra or model runtime issues.
acceptance_criteria: PRD and canary runbook reviewed and approved by Research, SRE, and Security (sign-offs recorded).
Prompt set created and validated (labels, golden outputs) and stored in the versioned prompt repo.
Automated evaluation pipeline implemented that can run full prompt set in <= 6 hours for batch candidates and quick-check subset in <= 20 minutes.
Alerting rules and automated rollback playbook implemented and tested in staging with simulated failures.
A/B experiment framework supports weighted scoring and multi-metric gating with configurable MDEs and alpha levels.
Sign-off from Customer Reliability Engineering that rollback does not violate data retention or privacy policies.
notes: 2026-03-03: Research spike showed hallucination detection model has 85% precision at current thresholds; we will add human review for alerts with medium confidence.
Tradeoffs discussed: tighter hallucination thresholds reduce rollouts but increase false positives and manual reviews; we picked a conservative default with escalation channels.
Implementation owner: Research (prompt tagging), SRE (pipeline + alerts), Releases (traffic routing automation).
